title.narrative: Réponse Humanitaire Multisectorielle d'Urgence pour les Populations Déplacées et Retournées dans les Zones de Santé de Kayna, Lubero, et Alimbongo Sud, Nord-Kivu

description.narrative: This project aims to provide multi-sectoral life-saving assistance to newly displaced and returnee populations in southern Lubero, North Kivu province, where the humanitarian situation has seriously deteriorated following the advance of the M23. Massive displacement has resulted in critical humanitarian needs. In terms of nutrition, UNICEF will monitor and treat 6,845 children suffering from acute malnutrition, in line with WHO 2023 guidelines. Counselling sessions will also be provided to pregnant and lactating women to improve infant feeding practices. The WASH intervention aims to improve access to water, hygiene, and sanitation for 32,500 people by rehabilitating water points, constructing emergency latrines, and conducting awareness campaigns. In child protection, approximately 8,475 children and their parents will benefit from adapted care, with particular attention paid to mental health, family reunification, and assistance to survivors of gender-based violence (GBV). Holistic assistance will be provided to 150 GBV survivors, and 3,000 girls and women will have access to GBV risk prevention and mitigation services. This crisis has also led to the destruction of schools, the flight of qualified teachers, and school dropouts, particularly affecting displaced children, children with disabilities, and adolescents. Approximately 55,503 displaced school-age children from Kayina, Alimbongo, and Lubero have settled in these areas, and the closure of 6 schools has affected the schooling of 3,600 children, less than a month before the start of the 2024-2025 school year. UNICEF will meet the educational needs of 3,670 people, including children, teachers, and principals, through the distribution of school and hygiene kits, the installation of temporary learning spaces, catch-up classes, and teacher training.
